---
title: "How certain is it?"
---

The [rules](rules.qmd) give one answer. `explain()`, and `--detail` on the command line, show
what that answer rests on: what each given name says in the register, what the last name's
suffix says, and whether they agree.

```bash
icename-gender name "Helga Ingimundarson" --detail
```

```
female	given_name (Helga)
  Helga           register  female
  Ingimundarson   suffix    male
  agreement: conflicting (female 1, male 1, unisex 0, unknown 0)
```

## Evidence

One line per part of the name:

| Source | Part | Says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `register` | each given name | `female`, `male`, `unisex`, or `unknown` |
| `suffix` | the last name, if it ends in *-dóttir* or *-son* | `female` or `male` |

A given name is `unknown` when the register does not list it, or lists it only as a middle
name. A hyphenated name not registered whole says what its registered parts say, or `unisex`
if they disagree.

## Agreement

| Agreement | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unanimous` | every part that says anything says the same |
| `conflicting` | some parts say female and some male; the estimate follows the rules |
| `none` | no part says female or male; the estimate is unknown |

`conflicting` is not an error. *Helga Ingimundarson* is a woman with a *-son* family name,
and the estimate is right. But a study that wants only the clearest cases can keep
`unanimous` rows and report how many it set aside.

## In a CSV

```bash
icename-gender csv people.csv --detail -o people_gender.csv
```

adds three columns to `gender` and `gender_rule`:

| Column | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `gender_agreement` | `unanimous`, `conflicting` or `none` |
| `gender_female` | how many parts say female |
| `gender_male` | how many parts say male |
